To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the CNNs are able to learn a representation of images that is more effective than the state of the art CBIR techniques.
1) the use of CNN in CBIR systems is beneficial, 2) the use of RF is beneficial for the performance, and 3) fine tuning the CNN with user feedback is beneficial.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following aspects: (a) the use of CNN for the retrieval process, (b) the use of RF for the tuning of CNN, (c) the exploitation of the tuned CNN in order to return the most relevant images.
the design and implementation of novel CBIR systems based on the exploitation of CNNs, which can also be easily integrated into existing systems.
the design and implementation of an innovative CBIR system based both on a CNN trained on large scale image databases, and on an RF mechanism where a CNN is updated according to the user's feedback.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our approach can improve CBIR performances in terms of retrieval precision.
the proposed approach can be used as a powerful tool for improving the performances of a CBIR system.
the proposed approach is a very good starting point for further research, and it can be easily integrated with other state of the art approaches to improve the performances in the CBIR task.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a novel CBIR system that exploits the generic image representation learned by a CNN and then fine tunes it by means of RF supplied by the users.
the proposed CBIR system is able to provide the user with images that are similar to her initial query, and that are also relevant to her needs, as they are obtained exploiting the user RF.

, in this paper, we propose a novel approach to improve the performances in CBIR by exploiting the generic image representations learned by CNNs and then re training the CNNs with a set of labelled images.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CNN can be successfully employed in CBIRs, especially when RF is employed.
the proposed CBIR system based upon transfer learning from CNNs can provide a significant improvement in the retrieval performances, especially in the context of RF.
, when a RF mechanism is employed, CNNs can be successfully used to improve the performances and reduce the semantic gap of a CBIR system.
